e7d9357d13840baf41b6c3a0a5a43cacb7209fcc.summary: Trend Micro reports that the Pawn Storm cyber-espionage campaign used a new Adobe Flash zero-day, tracked as CVE-2015-7645, in spear phishing emails aimed at several foreign affairs ministries. The lure emails used news-themed subjects. The report says the flaw affects Flash Player versions 19.0.0.185 and 19.0.0.207, and that Adobe released bulletin APSB15-27 to address it. Related tactics included fake Outlook Web Access servers for credential phishing and a compromised DNS setting at one ministry. The article was published 2015-10-13 and updated through October 2015.

e7b50fe20edcbd0eaeb0db26485e1edeb347845f.summary: News report on CaddyWiper, a destructive wiper that ESET observed in Ukraine, seen on a few dozen systems at a limited number of organizations. It erases user data and partition information and spares domain controllers, which ESET says is probably a way for attackers to keep access. Symantec and ESET first saw wiper malware in February, with Trojan.Killdisk deployed before Russian forces crossed the border. CrowdStrike reported misuse of EaseUS Partition Master drivers. Other researchers named the malware DriveSlayer. CISA issued an advisory.
